skill.name: code-analysis
skill.description: Analyze source files for readability by non-developers, including naming, comments, jargon, documentation, and readability score.
skill.summary: Check code readability for managers, stakeholders, and new team members.
skill.author: abereyes

content.value_statement: Teams often need code that managers, stakeholders, and new contributors can understand. This skill checks naming, comments, jargon, and documentation so reviewers get a clear readability score.
actual_capabilities: Runs a local Python analyzer against supported source files.
Scores readability from 0 to 100 with a plain English summary.
Flags cryptic variable names, unclear abbreviations, and single-letter assignments.
Checks comment coverage and long code sections without explanation.
Detects unexplained technical jargon in comments.
Reports missing What, Why, and How documentation near functions and classes.
limitations: It only analyzes file types listed in analyze.py.
It uses pattern checks, so some findings need human judgment.
It reads local files but does not understand project architecture deeply.
It cannot rewrite code unless the user asks for separate edits.

use_cases.title: Review Stakeholder-Facing Code
use_cases.description: Check whether important files use names and comments that non-developers can follow before a review meeting.

use_cases.title: Prepare New Contributor Onboarding
use_cases.description: Find unclear names and missing explanations before sharing code with a new team member.

use_cases.title: Improve Documentation Habits
use_cases.description: Use the findings to add useful comments and reduce unexplained jargon during regular development.

prompt_templates.title: Check One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-analysis skill to review this file for non-developer readability: [path]. Use standard strictness.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [path] with focus on comments. Summarize missing explanations and suggest the three most useful comment improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Strictness Levels
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a readability review on [path] with lenient and strict settings. Compare score changes and explain which findings are worth fixing.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Review Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [path] for a stakeholder handoff. Prioritize naming, jargon, and missing What, Why, and How documentation in a concise action plan.

output_examples.output: Readability score: 78/100. Main issues: several abbreviations need clearer names, and one long section needs an explanatory comment.

output_examples.input: Check onboarding script with strict settings.
output_examples.output: Strict review found missing What, Why, and How notes near helper functions. The file is understandable but needs clearer purpose statements.

output_examples.input: Focus on comments for a TypeScript file.
output_examples.output: The comments explain basic steps but not the business reason. Add short notes before validation and error handling sections.

best_practices: Review one file at a time when you need precise line-level feedback.
Use strict mode before stakeholder reviews or onboarding documentation.
Treat the score as a guide and confirm suggestions with project context.
anti_patterns: Do not use the score as the only basis for code approval.
Do not analyze generated files unless you expect noisy results.
Do not ask the skill to judge security, performance, or business correctness.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes naming, comments, jargon, documentation, and readability scoring for supported source files.

faq.question: Who is it for?
faq.answer: It helps developers make code easier for managers, stakeholders, and new team members to understand.

faq.question: Does it change my code?
faq.answer: No. It reports issues and suggestions. Code edits require a separate instruction.

faq.question: Which files can it read?
faq.answer: It supports Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, TSX, Java, Go, Ruby, and PHP files.

faq.question: Can I get machine-readable results?
faq.answer: Yes. The analyzer supports a JSON output option for scripts and tooling.

faq.question: Is this a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on readability, not vulnerabilities, secrets, or dependency risk.
